routes.title: Systems engineering fundamentals
routes.subtitle: Make defensible system boundaries, discover stakeholder value, and express obligations before design.

stages.title: Understand the problem
stages.goal: Distinguish the system of interest, its interfaces, and whose needs matter.
stages.check: What belongs inside the boundary, and whose outcomes could be omitted?

stages.title: From needs to measurable obligations
stages.goal: Turn operational scenarios into verifiable requirements and performance measures.
stages.check: Can an engineer test the proposed obligation without interpreting intent?

stages.title: Control and defend the baseline
stages.goal: Recognize uncertainty and establish a versioned technical management baseline.
stages.check: Which claim changes when the baseline changes, and who authorizes that change?

routes.title: Architecture and model-based engineering
routes.subtitle: Move from functional concepts to credible models, interfaces, allocations and traceable digital evidence.

stages.title: Understand model viewpoints
stages.goal: Separate functions from implementation and select views with a defined purpose.
stages.check: What question does each view answer, and what does it deliberately omit?

stages.title: Allocate responsibilities
stages.goal: Define allocations, contracts and object behavior that can be checked together.
stages.check: Could two different teams interpret the same interface differently?

stages.title: Connect the evidence
stages.goal: Preserve typed trace links, digital-thread meaning and trustworthy technical data lineage.
stages.check: Can a reviewer reproduce which model baseline supported a decision?

routes.title: Verification, test and assurance
routes.subtitle: Find out what can be claimed from tests, observations, proofs, hazard controls and limitations.

stages.title: Understand evidence and human use
stages.goal: Distinguish verification from validation while preparing human-centered test objectives.
stages.check: What would pass a specification but fail in real operation?

stages.title: Measure and prove carefully
stages.goal: Use traceable measurements, statistical acceptance and formal properties while accounting for hazards.
stages.check: Which uncertainties or unmodeled behaviors could invalidate acceptance?

stages.title: Integrate qualification evidence
stages.goal: Compare laboratory evidence with operational conditions and build a claim-based decision.
stages.check: What evidence would a skeptical independent reviewer still need?

routes.title: Simulation, uncertainty and decisions
routes.subtitle: Model mechanisms and uncertainty before making comparative design or investment choices.

stages.title: Model the decision, not the software
stages.goal: Identify uncertain inputs, intended use and the operational queues that shape performance.
stages.check: What quantity must the model predict for this decision to be useful?

stages.title: Build and challenge simulation evidence
stages.goal: Study event flow and feedback, then verify models and design interpretable experiments.
stages.check: Do the results change when you perturb plausible assumptions?

stages.title: Make defensible choices under uncertainty
stages.goal: Compare options using preference models, Pareto frontiers, information value and robust criteria.
stages.check: Which alternative remains defensible if priorities or conditions change?

routes.title: Software, delivery and sustainment
routes.subtitle: Deliver trustworthy software-intensive systems and keep them usable over their full lifecycle.

stages.title: Quality, evidence and reliability
stages.goal: Understand quality tradeoffs, deployment evidence and sustained service performance.
stages.check: Can a successful release still be operationally unreliable?

stages.title: Control change and threats
stages.goal: Adapt delivery processes, trace configuration changes and engineer trust boundaries.
stages.check: How would you prove that the tested version is the deployed version?

stages.title: Plan long-term support
stages.goal: Address supplier provenance, life-cycle costs and inevitable technology refresh.
stages.check: What hidden support dependencies could dominate the acquisition price?

routes.title: Systems of systems and enterprise complexity
routes.subtitle: Reason about autonomous actors, governance, feedback, resilience and adaptive intervention.

stages.title: Understand autonomous constituents
stages.goal: Characterize systems of systems and use mission threads to expose interdependence.
stages.check: Which constituent can refuse an integration change, and what then?

stages.title: Make authority and emergence visible
stages.goal: Connect governance, enterprise incentives and nonlinear behavior.
stages.check: Who can authorize a change, and who bears consequences?

stages.title: Intervene with evidence and humility
stages.goal: Analyze resilience, improvement claims and how interventions create new feedback.
stages.check: What observation would cause you to reverse an intervention?

model: Advisory prerequisites; progression reflects reader-confirmed study, not assessment. No new assignments.
